Modified assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- Decision and tone: Balanced-hawkish hold. The FOMC kept the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50% and continued QT. Floor-system settings (IOER 5.4%, ON RRP 5.3%, standing repo 5.5%) maintain control of short-term rates. The statement remains highly attentive to inflation risks.
- SLOOS overlay: Banks report broad-based tightening in lending standards and terms across C&I and CRE, as well as consumer credit (credit cards and auto), with weaker loan demand. Large banks cite deposit outflows, liquidity positions, higher funding costs, and declines in the market value of fixed-income assets; foreign banks emphasize credit quality, the economic outlook, collateral values, and loan market liquidity. Residential categories (RRE/HELOCs, QM and non-QM segments) also show tighter standards. These developments confirm that financial and credit conditions have tightened materially.
- Implications: SLOOS tightening amplifies the expected drag on activity and hiring mentioned in the statement, reinforcing a cautious, data-dependent stance even as Q3 growth was strong and the banking system is described as sound. Net tone shifts slightly more negative versus a resilience-only read, given elevated inflation alongside a restrictive credit channel.
